title: Phase formation in pinless friction stir spot welding of DP600 dual-phase steel to 6061 aluminum alloy dissimilar joints
abstract: AA6061 alloy sheets have been successfully joined to dual-phase DP600 steel sheets using the pinless friction stir spot welding (P-FSSW) technique. The interfacial microstructural characteristics and phase transformation processes were examined through scanning electron microscopy (SEM) coupled with an energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) system. A thermodynamic model was used to determine the formation sequence of AlFe intermetallic phases at the faying interface, based on simulated thermal cycle results obtained through finite element analysis (using ABAQUS software). Based on the maximum interface temperature of 527 °C, derived from numerical simulations, Fe4Al13and Fe2Al5 were identified as the primary and secondary phases, respectively. Furthermore, the growth kinetics of the intermetallic compound layer within the interfacial region of the joint were investigated and linearly fitted by a parabolic relationship between welding time and intermetallic phase thickness, expressed as x = 3.77 t0.5, providing a reliable predictive tool to tailor layer thickness. These insights not only validate P-FSSW as a low-distortion, energy-efficient technique for dissimilar-metal assembly but also deliver actionable guidelines for optimizing joint integrity in lightweight transportation and structural applications.
